ChromeSunder.Tier2: The implant is Damaged, and the target is bleeding heat — the Director may call a biofeedback jolt.
ChromeSunder.Tier3: The implant is Destroyed. Its benefit is gone and its Body Integrity is locked out until the wreck is repaired or replaced. The implant is not removed from the body.
ChromeSunder.Effect_before0000000000:
Pick one implant the target is carrying. Ghostwire opens the Chrome strike prompt when the use card posts, and never deletes the Item — a Destroyed implant stays in the flesh, benefits dead, Integrity spent.

Grade matters: Soft chrome takes one step less; Salvage chrome one step more. At the table, one implant per target may be Destroyed per encounter.
ChromeSunder.Effect_spend00000000000: 5 Resonance. You take the Director’s biofeedback for tearing a machine apart from inside a living body: a hard Physique test, and on a failure [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina. Resonance Mending is the answer to this ability, including on your own crew.

DecompileSprite.Name: Decompile Sprite
DecompileSprite.Story: You let the loop close. The sprite unspools back into the wire it was cut from, and the Bandwidth it was holding comes home.
DecompileSprite.Effect_before0000000000: Choose one sprite you have compiled, or all of them. Each chosen sprite is decompiled: its token leaves the encounter and the Bandwidth it held is yours again.

UndercityBarrens.Name: Undercity Barrens
UndercityBarrens.Description:
You grew up below the city’s foundations — flooded transit tunnels, collapsed arcades, and squatter blocks the corps wrote off decades ago. Down there you learned who runs each tunnel and how to move without being noticed.

Skills: you gain Stealth, and choose one of Streetwise, Survival, Perception, or Athletics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know the Undercity’s squatter blocks, tunnel gangs, and scavenger crews. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

CorpArcology.Name: Corp Arcology
CorpArcology.Description:
You were raised inside a megacorp arcology — company school, company clinic, company everything. You know how departments really work and how to talk your way up a chain of command.

Skills: you gain Corporate, and choose one of Persuasion, Negotiation, Insight, or Security Systems. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know your arcology’s departments, company families, and internal security. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

SprawlDistrict.Name: Sprawl District
SprawlDistrict.Description:
You came up in the endless mid-city Sprawl, where every block has its own fixer, its own gang tax, and its own price for everything. You learned to haggle before you learned to read.

Skills: you gain Streetwise, and choose one of Negotiation, Contacts, Perception, or Brawl. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know your district’s street vendors, fixers, block associations, and local gangs. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

TransitHub.Name: Transit Hub / Freeport
TransitHub.Description:
You grew up where everything moves: a maglev terminus, a cargo freeport, or an orbital elevator’s base. Everyone passes through, everyone owes someone, and you know every route in and out.

Skills: you gain Navigation, and choose one of Contacts, Driving, Piloting, or Negotiation. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know dockworkers, freight crews, customs brokers, and travelers passing through your hub. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

OutlandWastes.Name: Outland Wastes
OutlandWastes.Description:
You’re from beyond the city walls — dead farmland, toxic scrub, and nomad convoys between ruined towns. You’re hard to kill and you know how to keep going when the water runs out.

Skills: you gain Survival, and choose one of Athletics, Driving, Perception, or Firearms. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know Outland nomad clans, convoy runners, and wasteland settlements. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

AcademicSpire.Name: Academic Spire
AcademicSpire.Description:
You were raised among a university or research spire’s archives and restricted stacks, where old histories and older forbidden texts sit side by side. You learned what the official record leaves out.

Skills: you gain History, and choose one of Occult, Matrix Theory, Medicine Lore, or Xenology. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know your spire’s faculty, archivists, research departments, and rival scholars. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

FaithDistrict.Name: Faith District
FaithDistrict.Description:
You grew up in the shadow of a cathedral of the Light — shelters, soup lines, confessionals, and street preachers. You learned the dogma, and you learned to read the desperate people who came looking for it.

Skills: you gain Religion, and choose one of Insight, Occult, Warding, or Medicine. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know the district’s churches, shelters, orders of the Light, and the faithful who depend on them. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

IndustrialDeep.Name: Industrial Deep
IndustrialDeep.Description:
You come from the foundries, mines, and reactor levels under the city — Corran labor towns most often, but open to anyone who grew up on shift work. You can keep any machine running with scrap and stubbornness.

Skills: you gain Engineering, and choose one of Repair, Athletics, Demolitions, or Electronics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know foundry crews, labor unions, and Industrial Deep shift towns. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

WageSlave.Name: Wage-Slave
WageSlave.Description:
You worked a corporate desk job — cubicle hives, quarterly targets, and contracts you weren’t allowed to read. You know the system from the bottom and how to bargain your way through it.

Skills: you gain Negotiation, and choose two of Corporate, Persuasion, Insight, or Electronics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

StreetDoc.Name: Street Doc
StreetDoc.Description:
You patched up people who couldn’t go to a real clinic: gunshot wounds, back-alley chrome, and overdoses, no questions asked. You learned to read a patient who’s lying about how they got hurt.

Skills: you gain Medicine, and choose two of Cybertech, Insight, Streetwise, or Medicine Lore. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Fixer.Name: Fixer
Fixer.Description:
You connected people who needed things done with people who could do them, and took your cut. Your commlink is the most valuable thing you own.

Skills: you gain Contacts, and choose two of Negotiation, Streetwise, Insight, or Deception. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Courier.Name: Courier
Courier.Description:
You moved packages that couldn’t go through the mail — data chips, cash, sometimes things that were still breathing. Fast, quiet, and never late.

Skills: you gain Driving, and choose two of Stealth, Navigation, Athletics, or Streetwise. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

GangSoldier.Name: Gang Soldier
GangSoldier.Description:
You held a corner for a gang: collecting protection money, running off rivals, and shooting when talking stopped working.

Skills: you gain Firearms, and choose two of Intimidation, Streetwise, Brawl, or Melee. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

SecurityGuard.Name: Security Guard
SecurityGuard.Description:
You stood post for a corp, a mall, or a private security contractor. Long hours watching cameras and doorways taught you to spot trouble before it starts.

Skills: you gain Perception, and choose two of Firearms, Intimidation, Security Systems, or Brawl. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Smuggler.Name: Smuggler
Smuggler.Description:
You moved contraband past checkpoints and scanners — bypassing seals, forging manifests, and knowing which inspector could be paid.

Skills: you gain Security Systems, and choose two of Deception, Contacts, Driving, or Stealth. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

RigTech.Name: Rig-Tech
RigTech.Description:
You maintained and flew drones and remote vehicles for a delivery firm, a security company, or a salvage crew, jacked into the rig.

Skills: you gain Rigging, and choose two of Electronics, Repair, Driving, or Piloting. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

DeckJockey.Name: Deck Jockey
DeckJockey.Description:
You made a living in the Wired: freelance intrusion work, data brokering, or corp pen-testing. You built your own deck and you know how the network actually thinks.

Skills: you gain Hacking, and choose two of Matrix Theory, Electronics, Security Systems, or Streetwise. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Entertainer.Name: Entertainer
Entertainer.Description:
You performed for a living — club stages, simstim streams, or street-corner shows. You know how to work a crowd and how to be whoever the audience wants.

Skills: you gain Performance, and choose two of Persuasion, Deception, Insight, or Contacts. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

BeatReporter.Name: Beat Reporter
BeatReporter.Description:
You chased stories for a newsfeed until one got too close to a corp that didn’t want it told. You notice details, you know how companies hide things, and you have sources everywhere.

Skills: you gain Perception, and choose two of Corporate, Contacts, Insight, or Electronics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Hauler.Name: Hauler / Labor
Hauler.Description:
You drove freight rigs, loaded cargo, or worked heavy labor crews. Hard work, long hauls, and keeping old trucks alive.

Skills: you gain Athletics, and choose two of Driving, Repair, Brawl, or Engineering. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

MercRecruit.Name: Merc Recruit
MercRecruit.Description:
You signed with a private military company or a free company and did a tour in someone else’s war zone. You learned to shoot, march, and survive in the field.

Skills: you gain Firearms, and choose two of Athletics, Survival, Melee, or Heavy Weapons. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Acolyte.Name: Acolyte
Acolyte.Description:
You served an order of the Light (or a less reputable faith) — rites, exorcisms, and the long nights listening to people confess what they’d seen in the dark.

Skills: you gain Occult, and choose two of Religion, Insight, Warding, or Rituals. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

ChopDocAssistant.Name: Chop-Doc Assistant
ChopDocAssistant.Description:
You assisted a black-clinic chop-doc: holding patients down, sterilizing salvaged chrome, and knowing which gang would pay for which part.

Skills: you gain Cybertech, and choose two of Medicine, Streetwise, Demolitions, or Electronics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

WardApprentice.Name: Ward Apprentice
WardApprentice.Description:
You apprenticed under a society ward — Measure Collegium chalk-lines, Wickkeeper hearth-rights, or an Ash Survey field seal — learning to hold a threshold when the Veil thins.

Skills: you gain Warding, and choose two of Occult, Insight, Religion, or Rituals. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: society letters of introduction, a chalk kit or wick-tin, and the habit of checking doors twice.

Magical Profession (G5). Does not invent a fourth magic source — you serve an existing Reach society craft.

SurveyHand.Name: Survey Hand
SurveyHand.Description:
You walked Ash Survey grids and Veil craft perimeter walks — sampling grit, tagging bleed sites, and filing what the street pretends not to see.

Skills: you gain Perception, and choose two of Survival, Occult, Streetwise, or Insight. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: a field slate, sample vials, and a reputation for coming back with receipts.

Magical Profession (G5). Street-facing survey craft under existing society umbrellas — not a new magic source.

RitualWardTheRoom.Name: Formula: Ward the Room
RitualWardTheRoom.Description:
Ritual Formula · Ward · Magnitude 1 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Ward · Magnitude 1 · General

Formula Item form: ritual scroll (Veil path) · datachip (Wire-chalk skin)

The story: You walk the edges of one room laying a line of blessed salt along the threshold and burning resin in the corners until the air goes still. Anything on the other side of the Veil that tries to lean in finds the room hard to look at.

In plain words: Ghosts, spirits and any magic aimed into the room from outside get a bane — one penalty die on the roll. It does not stop people, bullets, cameras or hackers at all.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Magnitude 1 is the smallest Working there is: one room, one night, one bane. Bigger wards in this family cover more ground, last longer, or hit harder.
  • Scope — One room. Only Veil things — spirits and magic. Sprites, Agents, ICE and Wire snooping walk straight through it; for those, lay Data Ward.
  • Seal — One evening's work and one roll at the end. Low: it hangs — the Director holds a half-finished ward that may go off wrong. Middle: the ward is up. High: the ward is up and the cost of making it is blunted one step.
  • Expires — At the next dawn (or the next dusk, if you sealed it at night — pick when you seal). Breaking the salt line ends it early.

Payoff: One room gets a Veil barrier. Spirits and Magic-keyword / Veil remote targeting take a bane to enter or pierce it. People, bullets, and ordinary sensors pass as normal — it is not a wall. This is the teaching floor of the Ward family; bigger wards cover more space, last longer, or bite harder.

Duration / upkeep: Until the next dawn (or dusk, if sealed at night — pick at sealing). No upkeep.

Scope notes: Veil only — spirits and Magic-keyword peeks. Does not hinder sprites, Agents, ICE, or pure Overlay / Jacked-In verbs, even with the Wire-chalk skin. For Wire protection lay Data Ward.

Combat translation: Ambient bane on Veil verbs into or through the room. No summon, no wall against bullets. If a fight starts inside, the ward keeps working on Veil verbs until broken. No pool spend.

Study time: 1 day.

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 2.
  • Components: not a Project — pick one path. Components total ¥75 (Veil path) / ¥40 (Wire-chalk skin) (table below).
  • Sanctum: temporary — the room itself (¥0). No Project.

Components

Component Path Availability ¥
Blessed salt (threshold line) Veil Street 25
Resin incense Veil Street 50
Circuit-chalk (glyph dust) Wire-chalk skin Street 40
Thin-place ash (optional) any Fetch / mission —
Components total — Veil path ¥75
Components total — Wire-chalk skin ¥40

Sealing: one downtime evening. Price: negligible; spirit-attention +1 if sealed in a thin place.

Counter: Break the salt line or chalk circle; Unmaking at Magnitude 1; dawn.

Shared ritual rules (study, components, sanctum, sealing, detection, countermagic): @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.rulebook.JournalEntry.lbVxCseGwPRNJsZL]{The Veil — Ritual Workings}.

RitualSealTheFlat.Name: Formula: Seal the Flat
RitualSealTheFlat.Description:
Ritual Formula · Ward · Magnitude 2 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Ward · Magnitude 2 · General

Formula Item form: ritual scroll (Veil path) · datachip (Wire-chalk skin)

The story: Three nights of work: salt at every door, chalk on every window, a mark scratched into each vent. When it is done the whole place feels like somebody is awake in it, even when nobody is.

In plain words: Every room, door, window and vent of one dwelling gets the same bane Ward the Room gives one room. The first time something Veil-side forces its way in, you wake up and know, wherever you are in the district.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Magnitude 2 buys the whole flat instead of one room, plus the alarm. It also means you need a sanctum rated 2 to seal it.
  • Scope — One dwelling, up to about six rooms — a Flats unit, a safehouse floor, a coffin-cube row. Veil only; for the flat's node lay Data Ward as well.
  • Seal — This card runs study, sanctum and sealing all as Projects — it is the worked example of the full chain. Low: hung, and the flat is not sealed. Middle: sealed. High: sealed, and one step of Price is blunted.
  • Expires — At the third dawn after sealing. Re-lay the thresholds before then (¥60 of salt, one evening, no roll) for three more dawns. Miss a renewal and it lapses — you start again at sealing, not at the beginning.

Seal the Flat is the full Project prototype: it is the one Magnitude 2 card that runs study, sanctum, and sealing as Projects, so a crew can see every stage move on a progress track.

Payoff: A whole flat — every room, door, window, and vent of one dwelling (a Flats unit, a safehouse floor, a coffin-cube row up to about 6 rooms) — gets a Veil barrier. Spirits and Magic-keyword / Veil remote targeting take a bane to enter or pierce any part of it. The first time something Veil-side pushes through (wins past the bane), the leader wakes or knows, wherever they are in the district. People, bullets, and ordinary sensors pass as normal — it is not a wall.

Duration / upkeep: Until the third dawn after sealing. Renewal: before that dawn, re-lay the thresholds (¥60 of blessed salt, one evening, no roll) for three more dawns. Miss a renewal and the seal lapses; start again from the sealing stage (the sanctum Project stays done while the crew lives there).

Scope notes: Veil only. Does not hinder sprites, Agents, ICE, or pure Overlay / Jacked-In verbs, even with the Wire-chalk skin. For Wire protection lay Data Ward on the flat's node too.

Combat translation: Ambient bane on Veil verbs into or through any part of the flat. No summon, no wall against bullets. If a fight starts inside, the seal keeps working until a counter breaks it. No pool spend.

Study time: 3 days.

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 4 (Project). Logic or Instinct; Rituals, Occult, or Religion (Matrix Theory for the Wire-chalk skin) gives its usual benefit.
  • Components: not a Project. Components total ¥180 (Veil path) / ¥150 (Wire-chalk skin) (table below).
  • Sanctum: goal 6 (Project) — the flat itself becomes the sanctum. Each roll cleanses and chalks one or two rooms: scrub the old stains out, map every opening, bless the corners. Roll Instinct, Logic, or Persona with Rituals, Occult, or Religion; anyone who lives there may assist (edge). Once done, the flat stays a rating 2 sanctum while the crew keeps living there — later Seal the Flat castings skip this stage.
  • Sealing: goal 4 (Project) — one threshold at a time, over evenings. Each sealing roll uses the leader's tradition characteristic (Persona for a Street Priest; Logic for an Elementalist; Logic with Matrix Theory for a Technomancer). The roll that reaches the goal sets the outcome (low / middle / high, see Sealing in the shared rules). Components are consumed on the first sealing roll.

Components

Component Path Availability ¥
Blessed salt (every threshold, window, and vent line) Veil Street 60
Resin incense (one stick per room) Veil Street 50
Lintel wax seals (four) Veil Street 40
Ward-thread (window and vent cords) Veil Street 30
Circuit-chalk (three tins) Wire-chalk skin Street 120
Conductive tape (window and vent lines) Wire-chalk skin Street 30
Thin-place ash (optional; edge on the final sealing roll) any Fetch / mission —
A key or lease from the flat's owner (optional; edge on the sanctum Project) any Fetch / mission —
Components total — Veil path ¥180
Components total — Wire-chalk skin ¥150

Price: light — spirit-attention +2 on the final sealing roll (+3 if the flat sits on a thin place). The neighbors smell incense for a week.

Counter: Break the salt line at every opening, or scrub the lintel seals; Unmaking at Magnitude 2; the third dawn without a renewal. Breaking one threshold opens only that doorway or window — the rest of the flat stays sealed.

Story walkthrough — Vessa seals the Ninth-and-Fold flat

  1. The need. After a loud job, the crew holes up in Vessa's two-room flat above Ninth-and-Fold. Something from the job followed them — a cold draft that moves against the wind, a mirror that fogs from the inside. Ward the Room would cover one room for one night. Vessa wants the whole flat, for days.
  2. Find. No stall sells this. A dying Shepherd deacon leaves Vessa a folded scroll of Seal the Flat in a hymnal. It goes on her sheet. It's loot until she studies it.
  3. Study (Project, goal 4). The Formula's study time is 3 days. Vessa rolls Instinct with Religion over two respites: a middle result (2), then another middle (2). Four progress, three days passed — the Director marks the Formula learned.
  4. Components (not a Project). The crew buys the Veil path at a Flats botanica: salt, incense, wax, thread. ¥180 comes off the crew fund in one hit.
  5. Sanctum (Project, goal 6). The flat has to be clean before it can be sealed. Vessa scrubs, chalks, and blesses room by room. The crew's Operator lives there too and assists (edge). Rolls: high (3), middle (2), low (1) — six progress. The flat is now a rating 2 sanctum.
  6. Sealing (Project, goal 4). Over two evenings, Vessa seals the thresholds: the front door and hall window first (Persona, middle — 2), then the back window and the bathroom vent (Persona with an assist, high — 3). Progress 5 meets the goal; the final roll was high, so the payoff lands clean and the Director blunts the Price to spirit-attention +1.
  7. Payoff. Until the third dawn, anything Veil-side takes a bane to push into any part of the flat. On the second night the cold draft hits the salt at the hall window, fails, and fades. The next evening Vessa spends ¥60 on salt to renew.
  8. What breaks it. A rival kicks the front-door line in: that door is open to spirits, the rest of the flat stays sealed. Or dawn number three with no renewal.

RitualStreetFocusCharm.Description:
Ritual Formula · Artifice · Magnitude 2 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Artifice · Magnitude 2 · General

Formula Item form: ritual scroll or slim chapbook

The story: You spend a night rubbing a stain, a sheen or a varnish into something you already carry — a focus, a knife, a deck — until it stops being just yours and starts being part of the work.

In plain words: One named magic (or Resonance) ability gets an edge — one bonus die — whenever you use it through that item. Or, instead, the item picks up one Veil tag for the run.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Magnitude 2 is charm-tier and that is the ceiling: there is no permanent version of this card. For a permanent implement you want Telesma Birth.
  • Scope — One item you already own, and one ability named when you seal it. It never gives you an ability you did not have.
  • Seal — One evening. Low: hung — no charm. Middle: the charm holds. High: it holds and Price is blunted one step.
  • Expires — At the end of the session, or at your next major respite — the Director picks which when you seal it.

Payoff: Bonds a short-run charm to one focus, light weapon, or deck-adjacent focus the leader already owns — elemental stain, pact sheen, or Wire varnish by tradition. One named Magic (or Resonance) ability gains an edge when used through that Item, or the Item gains a one-off Veil tag.

Duration / upkeep: One session, or until the next major respite (Director picks at sealing). No upkeep. Charm-tier only; no permanent version.

Scope notes: Works on the ability named at sealing; the tradition matches the leader. Doesn't create new abilities.

Combat translation: Gear flag — edge on the named ability. No pool spend to keep it. It fades when the duration ends, even mid-fight.

Study time: 3 days.

RitualRemoteSense.Name: Formula: Remote Sense
RitualRemoteSense.Description:
Ritual Formula · Reach · Magnitude 2 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Reach · Magnitude 2 · General

Formula Item form: datachip (Wire-native) or ritual scroll

The story: You sit still with your eyes shut and borrow somebody else's. A jacked-in friend, a tagged camera, a small spirit perched on a ledge — whatever is out there looking, you look through it.

In plain words: For one scene you see and hear whatever your spotter sees and hears, at any distance inside the printed Reach or Wired range.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Magnitude 2 is a one-scene borrow through a spotter who is already there. Reaching a target with no spotter needs a link Working (Hair-and-Wire, Keepsake, Effigy) on top.
  • Scope — You need a spotter at the far end. The link runs both ways: it can be traced back to you, and a bad seal or a won trace can reverse the pipe for a round — meaning they see you.
  • Seal — One evening. Low: hung, or the pipe points the wrong way. Middle: you get the scene. High: the scene, and Price blunted one step.
  • Expires — At the end of the scene, or the moment the link is cut — the spotter is knocked out, the camera dies, the trace wins.

Payoff: For one scene, the leader perceives through a spotter — an Overlay or Jacked-In ally, a tagged camera, or a minor spirit's eye — within the printed Reach or Wired range.

Duration / upkeep: One scene after sealing, or until the link is cut.

Scope notes: Needs a spotter present at the target (or a link Working — Hair-and-Wire, Keepsake, Effigy — if none). The link can be traced back; a failed seal or contested trace can reverse the pipe for a round.

Combat translation: A perception channel only — no summon, no strike. If knives come out mid-scene, the leader still just sees. No pool spend.

Study time: 3 days.

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 4.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥300 (table below).
  • Sanctum: temporary. No Project.

RitualWatcher.Name: Formula: Watcher
RitualWatcher.Description:
Ritual Formula · Calling · Magnitude 2 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Calling · Magnitude 2 · General

Formula Item form: ritual scroll; datachip for the Wire skin

The story: You call something small and patient and give it one job: sit here and tell me. It nests in a stairwell or a camera housing and does not move.

In plain words: A minor spirit or daemon guards a place you mark. When the condition you set is met, it tells you — once — and then waits for orders or fades. It never blocks or fights anything.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Magnitude 2 buys one small watcher and one warning. To get something that guards a place permanently you want Site Bind (Magnitude 4).
  • Scope — The marked site only. A Veil watcher sees spirits and people; a Wire daemon-watcher sees the node and its cameras. Neither one is a wall.
  • Seal — One evening. Low: hung — nothing arrives, or something arrives you did not ask for. Middle: the watcher is on post. High: on post, and Price blunted one step.
  • Expires — After hours equal to 4 × Persona (Street Priest) or 4 × Logic (Elementalist, Technomancer), or the moment you dismiss it.

Payoff: Calls a minor watcher-spirit, elemental extension, or (Wire skin) daemon-watcher to guard a marked site. It alerts the leader once when its trip condition is met, then waits for orders or fades.

Duration / upkeep: Hours equal to 4 × Persona (Street Priest) or 4 × Logic (Elementalist, Technomancer), or until dismissed. No upkeep.

Scope notes: A Veil watcher sees spirits and people; a daemon-watcher sees the node and its cameras. Neither blocks anything — it only warns.

Combat translation: Alert fiction or one free notice when the trip fires. Not a combat summon. If a later Working or the Director upgrades it to a figure, treat it as an extension (Summon Entities rules, The Veil) — usually untargetable. No pool spend.

Study time: 3 days.

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 4.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥220 (table below).
  • Sanctum: temporary — the marked site, claimed for one night. No Project.

Counter: Banish; Unmaking at Magnitude 2; kill it in a scene if it was upgraded to a figure.

RitualSiteBind.Name: Formula: Site Bind
RitualSiteBind.Description:
Ritual Formula · Calling · Magnitude 4 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Calling · Magnitude 4 · General

Formula Item form: tome / bound volume (bulky)

The story: You speak a name you were not supposed to learn, and something agrees to live in the walls. It knows every floorboard now. It was not asked politely.

In plain words: A named spirit, elemental or Wire-entity becomes the permanent guardian of a sanctum you have built. You must already know its name — from study, from Discover Lore, or from meeting it.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Magnitude 4 is heavy: it wants a sanctum rated 4, a night of sealing, and it moves faction clocks. Anyone Unmaking it has to beat Magnitude 4 and go through you.
  • Scope — It guards the site and nothing else. It does not come with you on a run unless your copy of the Formula says so. A Wire-entity guards the node side; a spirit guards the Veil side.
  • Seal — A night's work. Low: hung, and a named power now knows who called it. Middle: it is bound. High: bound, and Price blunted one step.
  • Expires — It does not — while the sanctum keystone stands and you keep paying the favour you owe. Break the keystone and it goes. Stop paying and the leash slips, which feeds Incursion and hands the Director Malice.

Payoff: Binds a named spirit, elemental, or Wire-entity as a permanent site guardian tied to a built sanctum. It knows the floorplan in its bones. The name must already be known (prior study, Discover Lore, or an encounter).

Duration / upkeep: While the sanctum keystone stands and the favor-debt is honored. A slipped leash feeds Incursion and Malice.

Scope notes: Guards the site only. It stays home when the crew runs elsewhere unless the Formula copy says otherwise. A Wire-entity guardian guards the node side; a spirit guards the Veil side.

Combat translation: When it fights on-site, it is an independent figure using the Summon Entities rules (The Veil) as a Stamina floor, run by the binder as a site asset. Not an encounter summon. Upkeep is favor and spirit-attention — no pool spend.

Study time: 2 weeks.

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 8.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥5,000 (table below).
  • Sanctum: built sanctum rating 4+ required — goal 12 (skip if the crew already owns one).

RitualCircleOfMany.Name: Formula: Circle of Many
RitualCircleOfMany.Description:
Ritual Formula · Other · Magnitude 2–4 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Other · Magnitude 2–4 · General

Formula Item form: ritual scroll (instructions) or a lodge tome chapter

The story: Chalk stations on the floor, one body at each of them, and a chant nobody in the room is good enough to carry alone.

In plain words: This does nothing by itself. It supports a different Working: every assistant station turns into an edge on that Working's sealing roll, or into extra Project progress toward it. A very big circle may let the Director raise one sealing's Magnitude ceiling by 1.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Your copy is written at one Magnitude between 2 and 4. The higher it is, the more stations it can hold and the more heat it draws.
  • Scope — It only ever helps another card. Non-casters can hold stations, which is the point — the whole crew can be in this one.
  • Seal — The circle is sealed as part of the night it supports. Low: a station fails and the circle fights the Working. Middle: the edges land. High: the edges land and Price is blunted a step.
  • Expires — At the end of the sealing night or Project block it was built for. The chalk marks stay on the floor until somebody cleans them.

Payoff: Formal multi-caster circle. Each assistant station becomes a sealing edge or adds Project progress on the Working the circle supports. A very large circle may ask the Director for +1 Magnitude ceiling on one sealing.

Duration / upkeep: For the sealing night or Project block it supports. The circle marks linger as fiction until cleaned.

Scope notes: Supports another Working; does nothing on its own. Non-casters matter here. Heat scales with Magnitude and headcount.

Combat translation: None — a downtime or climax beat. If interrupted mid-seal: backlash, components lost, Malice tick.

Study time: 3 days (Magnitude 2) · 1 week (Magnitude 3) · 2 weeks (Magnitude 4).

Project Points (stages):

  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥200 (Magnitude 2) / ¥800 (Magnitude 3) / ¥3,000 (Magnitude 4) (table below).
  • Sanctum: uses the supported Working's sanctum. No separate Project.

RitualExclusiveCharterRite.Description:
Ritual Formula · Other · Magnitude 3 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Other · Magnitude 3 · General

Formula Item form: bound volume (charter book), with member-list fields

The story: A lodge writes its own name into its Formulas, so that a stolen copy reads like a recipe with the verbs missing.

In plain words: One Working — or a small list of them — can only be led and sealed by members of your charter. Anyone outside it takes a bane on the sealing roll, and stolen copies go blurry in their hands.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Magnitude 3 sets the strength of the lock: Unmaking it needs Magnitude 3 or better.
  • Scope — It governs who may use the chartered Formulas. It does not protect the physical book from being taken — only from being useful.
  • Seal — A night's work. Low: hung, and the charter is readable by anyone until you try again. Middle: locked. High: locked, Price blunted a step.
  • Expires — Never, on its own. It ends when the charter is dissolved, Unmade, or when its living keys — the members whose names are in it — are all dead.

Payoff: Locks a Working (or a small slate of them) so only charter members can lead or seal it. Outsiders take a bane on sealing; copies go blurry for non-members.

Duration / upkeep: Permanent until the charter is broken or Unmade.

Scope notes: Affects who can use the chartered Formulas. Stolen copies become incomplete without membership.

Combat translation: None — a meta-asset on who runs rites. No tokens.

Study time: 1 week.

RitualLodgeKeystone.Name: Formula: Lodge Keystone
RitualLodgeKeystone.Description:
Ritual Formula · Ward · Magnitude 2–3 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Ward · Magnitude 2–3 · General

Formula Item form: tome (lodge prospectus), or engraved plaque with datachip backup

The story: A stone, a server rack or a beam gets carved, blessed and bolted in place, and the building around it stops being rented rooms and starts being yours.

In plain words: Your shared workspace becomes a permanent sanctum and its rating goes up by 1, to a maximum of 3 without further Projects. Sanctum rating is the gate on what Magnitude you are allowed to seal there. If your copy says so, the inside also gets a light ward — a bane on hostile spirits and magic peeks.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Your copy is written at Magnitude 2 or 3. Unmaking it has to beat the lodge's current rating, not the card's Magnitude.
  • Scope — Veil only. The ward-lite does nothing against Wire intrusion — lay Data Ward for that. Your Lifestyle band caps how high a rating the address can hold, whatever you spend.
  • Seal — A night's work, and a permanent ¥ upkeep after it. Low: hung — the keystone is inert stone. Middle: the rating goes up. High: the rating goes up and Price is blunted a step.
  • Expires — Never, while you pay the Lifestyle upkeep. Stop paying, or destroy the keystone, and the rating goes with it.

Payoff: Raises a shared lodge or group workspace as a permanent sanctum: +1 sanctum rating, capped at 3 unless further Projects and the Director open the ceiling. If the copy says so, the interior also carries a ward-lite (bane on hostile spirits and Magic peeks).

Duration / upkeep: Permanent, with Lifestyle upkeep ¥. Your Lifestyle band caps the rating the address can hold.

Scope notes: Veil ward-lite only. It doesn't stop Wire-only intrusion — lay Data Ward for that.

Combat translation: Ambient ward-lite bane inside the lodge, if printed; otherwise just a sanctum rating. No pool spend.

Study time: 3 days (Magnitude 2) · 1 week (Magnitude 3).

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 4 / 6.

RitualHairAndWireLink.Name: Formula: Hair-and-Wire Link
RitualHairAndWireLink.Description:
Ritual Formula · Reach · Magnitude 2–3 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Reach · Magnitude 2–3 · General

Formula Item form: scroll in a shielded tube, or encrypted datachip

The story: You need a piece of them. Hair, blood, a shard of a god-file, the core out of a deep handle. It is cold work and half the Reach will arrest you for it.

In plain words: Lets you aim a Reach Working at somebody with nobody standing near them. The remnant is the aim.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Your copy is written at Magnitude 2 or 3; the higher one reaches further and holds against a better-defended target.
  • Scope — Blood and tissue aim Veil Workings; handle cores and god-file shards aim Wire-rites. This leaves a much louder trace than Remote Sense through a live spotter, and a fake remnant fouls the seal — a bane, or backlash.
  • Seal — One evening, spent as part of the Working it aims. Low: the aim is wrong, or it points home. Middle: the aim holds. High: it holds and Price is blunted a step.
  • Expires — It powers exactly one following Reach sealing or scene, then it is spent. Destroying the remnant ends it early.

Payoff: Aims a Reach Working without a live spotter, using a strong remnant of the target — tissue, blood, a god-file shard, a deep handle core. Cold, intimate, illegal in half the Reach.

Duration / upkeep: Powers one following Reach sealing or scene.

Scope notes: Louder trace than Remote Sense with a spotter. A false remnant fouls the seal (bane or backlash). Blood and tissue aim Veil Workings; handle cores and god-file shards aim Wire-rites.

Combat translation: None as a summon. If used to peek into a fight, it's perception only unless chained to a separate strike Working. No pool spend.

Study time: 3 days (Magnitude 2) · 1 week (Magnitude 3).

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 4 / 6.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥300 (Magnitude 2) / ¥1,000 (Magnitude 3) (table below).

RitualKeepsakeLink.Name: Formula: Keepsake Link
RitualKeepsakeLink.Description:

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Reach · Magnitude 3 · General

Formula Item form: ritual scroll or slim sentimental booklet

The story: Not blood — a letter, a ring, a child's shoe, an archive nobody else kept. Things people love remember them.

In plain words: Aims a Reach Working through something the target treasures, when you cannot get anything off their body. Weaker than flesh and harder to seal, but it leaves an emotional trail anyone sensitive can follow.

  • Scope — One Reach payoff scene. Traceable like every Reach link: they can follow it back to you.

  • Expires — After one Reach payoff scene. Returning or destroying the keepsake ends it immediately.

Payoff: Aims a Reach Working through a beloved object or personal archive of the target. Weaker than flesh, harder to seal, louder emotional trace.

Duration / upkeep: One Reach payoff scene.

Scope notes: For when you can't get blood. Traceable like any Reach link.

Combat translation: None — a downtime and scene tool. No pool spend.

Study time: 1 week.

RitualEffigyLink.Description:

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Reach · Magnitude 3–4 · General

Formula Item form: tome with pattern plates, or datachip with fab instructions

The story: You build a small ugly version of the thing you mean to reach — a doll, a model of the flat, a double drawn in glyphs — and then you do to the model what you cannot get close enough to do for real.

In plain words: A stand-in that lets you aim a Reach or Unmaking Working across distance when you have no remnant and no keepsake. Scaffolding for the big remote Workings.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Your copy is written at Magnitude 3 or 4. A Magnitude 4 build is loud enough that faction clocks move just because you made it.
  • Scope — It aims other Workings; on its own it does nothing. Unmaking the link needs a Magnitude at least equal to the link's.
  • Seal — A night's craft. Low: the effigy is wrong and the Working it aims goes wrong with it. Middle: it aims true. High: it aims true and Price is blunted a step.
  • Expires — When it is spent on a sealing, or when somebody burns it.

Payoff: Builds a symbolic stand-in — a doll, a model flat, a glyph-double — to aim a Reach or Unmaking Working across distance. Ugly craft. Works when remnants and keepsakes fail.

Duration / upkeep: Until the effigy is spent on a sealing or destroyed.

Scope notes: Scaffolding for big remote Workings. Faction clocks notice Magnitude 4 builds.

RitualDoorSealGlyph.Description:
Ritual Formula · Ward · Magnitude 2 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Ward · Magnitude 2 · General

Formula Item form: ritual scroll or stencil-chip

The story: One glyph, cut into one door frame, small enough to miss. Spirits go around. So does the Wire.

In plain words: That single doorway refuses spirits, magic peeks and Wire bleed. It does nothing to flesh or bullets — those still only have to deal with the wood and the hinges.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Magnitude 2. Unmaking it needs Magnitude 2. Its strength is that it covers both sides — Veil and Wire — for a Magnitude that only buys one side elsewhere.
  • Scope — That one doorway. Walls, vents and every other door in the building are wide open.
  • Seal — One evening. Low: hung — the glyph is a scratch. Middle: the door is sealed. High: sealed, Price blunted a step.
  • Expires — When it is broken or Unmade, or at the expiry your copy prints — usually a number of dawns equal to its Magnitude, or for as long as you keep paying sanctum upkeep.

Payoff: One doorway refuses spirits, Magic peeks, and Wire bleed. Flesh and bullets still deal with the wood and hinges.

Duration / upkeep: Until broken or Unmade, or the expiry printed on the copy (often dawns equal to Magnitude, or while sanctum upkeep holds).

Scope notes: Covers both Veil and Wire bleed — but only through that one doorway. Walls, vents, and other doors are open.

Combat translation: Ambient bane (refusal) on Veil verbs and Wire bleed through the doorway. Breachers can still kick the physical door. No pool spend.

Study time: 3 days.

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 4.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥200 (table below).
  • Sanctum: temporary — the doorway. No Project.

Components

Component Availability ¥
Glyph paint or etch-acid Street 120
Threshold nails (four) Street 40
Frame salt Street 40
Components total ¥200

Counter: Scrape the glyph; Unmaking at Magnitude 2; destroy the door and scrub the frame.

Shared ritual rules (study, components, sanctum, sealing, detection, countermagic): @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.rulebook.JournalEntry.lbVxCseGwPRNJsZL]{The Veil — Ritual Workings}.

RitualChargedPerimeter.Name: Formula: Charged Perimeter
RitualChargedPerimeter.Description:
Ritual Formula · Ward · Magnitude 3 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Ward · Magnitude 3 · General

Formula Item form: tome section or engineer's datachip

The story: A ward that has been holding its breath. It does nothing at all until the wrong thing steps over the line, and then it lets go all at once.

In plain words: A silent ward that stores power and spends it in one go when it is crossed. What it does when it goes off is printed on your copy: a scream of an alarm, a stun pulse, a Malice tick, or some combination.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Magnitude 3 sets how hard it hits and what it takes to Unmake it. It is also loud enough to detect from further away than Ward the Room.
  • Scope — The perimeter you walked. Your copy names what trips it — spirits, magic peeks, named people, or (with the ICE-capacitor build) Wire intrusion.
  • Seal — A night's work. Low: hung — it may fire at the wrong thing, at the wrong time. Middle: it is armed. High: armed, and Price blunted a step.
  • Expires — The moment it discharges — once. Keep it charged instead with sanctum upkeep, paid in ¥ and reagents; it never costs a pool.

Payoff: A quiet ward that stores potency and spends it when crossed by the wrong kind of thing: an alarm scream, a stun pulse, and/or a Malice tick, as printed on the copy.

Duration / upkeep: Until it discharges once, or kept charged with sanctum upkeep (¥ and reagents — never pools).

Scope notes: The copy names the breach condition (spirits, Magic peeks, named people, Wire intrusion with the ICE-capacitor build). Louder to detect than Ward the Room.

Combat translation: Ambient until breached; on breach, the printed pulse or alarm fires once. No caster action or pool spend. Re-arming is a downtime Working, not an in-fight action.

Study time: 1 week.

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 6.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥1,400 (table below).
  • Sanctum: temporary — the warded perimeter. No Project.

Components

Component Availability ¥
Capacitor salts, prayer batteries, or ICE capacitors Restricted 900
Perimeter line (wire, chalk, or salt; about 40 squares) Professional 300
Trigger housing Professional 200
Breach-condition fetish (optional) Fetch / mission —
Components total ¥1,400

Counter: Discharge safely with Counterseal tools; Unmaking at Magnitude 3; send someone through to trip it.

Shared ritual rules (study, components, sanctum, sealing, detection, countermagic): @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.rulebook.JournalEntry.lbVxCseGwPRNJsZL]{The Veil — Ritual Workings}.

RitualReagentStill.Name: Formula: Reagent Still
RitualReagentStill.Description:
Ritual Formula · Artifice · Magnitude 1–2 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Artifice · Magnitude 1–2 · General

Formula Item form: scroll recipe or datachip

The story: A still in the back room, three days of dripping, and one small sealed pack of something that smells like a church and a battery at the same time.

In plain words: Makes a single-use reagent pack. Spend it at a later sealing and that sealing gets an edge, or its Price is blunted once — your call when you spend it.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Your copy is written at Magnitude 1 or 2; the Magnitude 2 version makes a stronger pack (your copy prints which).
  • Scope — It helps one later sealing. The pack is a separate item on the sheet — it can be stolen like anything else.
  • Seal — An evening. Low: hung, and the batch is spoiled. Middle: you get a pack. High: a pack, and Price blunted a step.
  • Expires — The pack lasts until it is used or until it spoils — usually one season or three sessions, printed on your copy.

Payoff: Distills a one-use reagent pack. Spent at a later sealing, it grants an edge on that sealing or blunts its Price once.

Duration / upkeep: The pack lasts until used or until it spoils (often one season or three sessions — printed).

Scope notes: Prep economy for big Workings. The pack is a separate consumable Item.

Combat translation: None — downtime craft. Using the pack is part of a sealing, not a combat action.

Study time: 1 day (Magnitude 1) · 3 days (Magnitude 2).

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 2 / 4.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥100 (Magnitude 1) / ¥250 (Magnitude 2) (table below).
  • Sanctum: temporary — the still. No Project.

Components

Component Availability Magnitude 1 Magnitude 2
Base solvents Street 60 150
Still rental (one night) Street 40 100
Uncommon flower, mineral, or code-seed Fetch / mission — —
Components total ¥100 ¥250

Counter: Spoil or steal the pack.

RitualTrueRelicCarve.Name: Formula: True Relic Carve
RitualTrueRelicCarve.Description:
Ritual Formula · Artifice · Magnitude 4–5 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Artifice · Magnitude 4–5 · General

Formula Item form: thick grimoire or fab-tome (bulky)

The story: Months of work on one object, and at the end of it you own something that has never existed before and that somebody will eventually kill you for.

In plain words: Carves a permanent prototype relic — a Restricted-or-better item with unique flags written by the Director. This is campaign gravity, not shopping. The Director can say no.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5. Magnitude 5 means the whole hive whispers about it: everybody with an ear in the Veil knows something was made.
  • Scope — The relic's own printed flags say whether it touches the Veil, the Wire, or both. Unbonding it needs Magnitude 4–5.
  • Seal — A night or a short climax scene. Low: hung, and a half-made relic is a liability. Middle: the relic exists. High: it exists and Price is blunted a step.
  • Expires — Never. It ends when it is destroyed, unbonded, corrupted, or when the doom clock printed on the relic itself runs out.

Payoff: Carves a permanent prototype relic (Restricted+) with unique flags. Director veto applies. Campaign gravity, not a shop item.

Duration / upkeep: Permanent until destroyed, unbonded, or corrupted.

Scope notes: The relic's flags say whether it touches Veil, Wire, or both. Magnitude 5 carries a hive-wide whisper.

Combat translation: Gear flags only. No ritual upkeep. If the relic grants a Persistent Magic ability, that ability uses its class Persistent math — never a ritual tax.

Study time: 2 weeks (Magnitude 4) · 1 month (Magnitude 5).

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 8 / 10.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥6,000 (Magnitude 4) / ¥16,000 (Magnitude 5) (table below).
  • Sanctum: built sanctum at the Working's Magnitude — goal 12 / 15 (skip if owned).

Components

Binding inlay (silver or chromed filament) Restricted / Military 2,000 6,000
Sealing lacquers Restricted / Military 1,500 4,000
Prototype blank (almost always a mission) Fetch / mission — —
A named spirit's or Wire blessing (favor) Fetch / mission — —
Components total ¥6,000 ¥16,000

Counter: Destroy the relic; unbond (Unmaking at Magnitude 4–5); the relic's printed doom clock.

RitualLongLeash.Name: Formula: Long Leash
RitualLongLeash.Description:
Ritual Formula · Calling · Magnitude 3–4 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Calling · Magnitude 3–4 · General

Formula Item form: bound service-contract tome or encrypted datachip

The story: Not a summoning — a contract. Something you already called agrees to keep doing small jobs for a while, and a tablet on your wall keeps the schedule.

In plain words: Binds an entity you have already called to intermittent services over days or weeks: carrying messages, standing watch, whispering, one dirty job. It does not mean "it fights beside me this round".

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Your copy is written at Magnitude 3 or 4. The higher copy holds a stronger entity and for longer.
  • Scope — Veil spirits and elementals. A Technomancer leading the Wire version should use Daemon Long Leash instead.
  • Seal — A night's work. Low: hung, and the entity is loose and annoyed. Middle: the leash holds. High: it holds and Price is blunted a step.
  • Expires — After the days or weeks you sealed it for. Renew it with another favour before then, or it lapses. Breaking the schedule tablet ends it at once.

Payoff: Long-term binding of an already-called entity for intermittent services over days or weeks — courier, watch, whisper, one dirty job. Not "wins this fight."

Duration / upkeep: Days to weeks as sealed. Renew with favor, or it lapses.

Scope notes: Spirit or elemental (Veil); a Technomancer leading the Wire skin should use Daemon Long Leash instead.

Combat translation: If present when knives come out: an extension by default (site helper), or independent if the copy says so, per the Summon Entities rules (The Veil). Stay inside the bound-count caps unless the Director agrees. Not encounter-summon spam. No pool spend.

Study time: 1 week (Magnitude 3) · 2 weeks (Magnitude 4).

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 6 / 8.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥1,300 (Magnitude 3) / ¥4,500 (Magnitude 4) (table below).
  • Sanctum: temporary at Magnitude 3; built sanctum rating 4 at Magnitude 4 — goal 12 (skip if owned).

Components

Component Availability Magnitude 3 Magnitude 4
Leash cord or schedule chip Restricted 700 2,500
Feeding stock (one month) Professional 400 1,200
Schedule tablet Professional 200 800
A prior successful Call or capture Fetch / mission — —
Special feeding offerings (optional) Fetch / mission — —
Components total ¥1,300 ¥4,500

Counter: Banish; break the schedule tablet; Unmaking at Magnitude 3–4.

Shared ritual rules (study, components, sanctum, sealing, detection, countermagic): @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.rulebook.JournalEntry.lbVxCseGwPRNJsZL]{The Veil — Ritual Workings}.

RitualTrueNameCollar.Name: Formula: True-Name Collar (Deep Bind)
RitualTrueNameCollar.Description:
Ritual Formula · Calling · Magnitude 4–5 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Calling · Magnitude 4–5 · General

Formula Item form: heavy grimoire (bulky) plus a sealed name-folio

The story: You say the name it was given before the world had people in it, and it stops. This is the card that gets characters killed.

In plain words: Collars an unbound named power — one nobody else has leashed — by its secret name or its deep handle. The Price is high and your copy prints the exact conditions under which it gets loose again.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5. Magnitude 5 moves faction clocks whether you wanted that or not.
  • Scope — Name-based. A true name collars a Veil power; a deep handle collars a Wire power (Technomancers have their own card, True-Handle Collar). It is contested by the thing you are collaring.
  • Seal — A night or a climax scene. Low: hung — and it now knows your name too. Middle: collared. High: collared, Price blunted a step.
  • Expires — When one of the escape conditions printed on your copy is met, when somebody Unmakes it at Magnitude 4–5, or when you die.

Payoff: Collars an unbound named power by its secret name or deep handle. High Price. The copy prints its escape conditions. Hubris with a warranty-void sticker.

Duration / upkeep: Until an escape condition, an Unmaking, or the binder's doom.

Scope notes: Name-based: a true name collars a Veil power; a deep handle collars a Wire power (Technomancers can also use True-Handle Collar). Magnitude 5 moves faction clocks whether you like it or not.

Combat translation: When forced into a fight: independent Stamina scaled to the named power (Director; floor at Rank 3+ elemental or independent spirit, Summon Entities rules). The binder commands only within the collar's terms. Escape mid-fight is a feature. No pool spend.

Study time: 2 weeks (Magnitude 4) · 1 month (Magnitude 5).

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 8 / 10.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥6,500 (Magnitude 4) / ¥19,000 (Magnitude 5) (table below).
  • Sanctum: built sanctum at the Working's Magnitude — goal 12 / 15 (skip if owned).

Components

Component Availability Magnitude 4 Magnitude 5
Collar forge materials Restricted / Military 4,000 12,000
Name-folio seal Restricted 1,500 4,000
Witness circle stations (Circle of Many) Restricted 1,000 3,000
The true name or deep handle (major quest) Fetch / mission — —
Components total ¥6,500 ¥19,000

Counter: The printed escape; Unmaking at Magnitude 4–5, contested; destroy the name-vessel.

RitualVesselDressing.Name: Formula: Vessel Dressing
RitualVesselDressing.Description:
Ritual Formula · Calling · Magnitude 3 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Calling · Magnitude 3 · General

Formula Item form: manual tome or tech datachip

The story: You prepare a body, a drone shell or a statue the way an undertaker prepares a room: washed, marked, and made ready for a guest.

In plain words: Makes something a legal vessel for a called entity to wear. Without it, possession is messy, hostile, or fatal to whoever is inside.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Magnitude 3. Unmaking the dressing — spoiling it before the guest arrives — needs Magnitude 3.
  • Scope — It enables clean possession, drone-rides and idol-walks for a later Calling. It does not call anything itself. The Technomancer version for Wire-entities is Chassis Dressing.
  • Seal — A night's work. Low: hung, and the vessel is a hazard. Middle: dressed and ready. High: ready, Price blunted a step.
  • Expires — When it is inhabited, or when the dressing spoils — usually days equal to its Magnitude, printed on your copy.

Payoff: Prepares a body, drone shell, or object as a legal vessel for a called entity to wear. Without this, inhabitation is messy, hostile, or lethal to the meat.

Duration / upkeep: Holds until inhabited, or spoils (often days equal to Magnitude — printed).

Scope notes: Enables clean possession, drone-rides, and idol-walks for later Callings. The Technomancer-only Chassis Dressing is the Wire-entity version.

Combat translation: An empty dressed vessel is a prop. Once inhabited, the rider uses the Summon Entities rules; a drone vessel keeps its machine Stamina (Machines chapter). No pool spend.

Study time: 1 week.

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 6.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥1,000 (table below).
  • Sanctum: temporary. No Project.

Components

Dressing oils, etch, or Wire permission-glyphs Professional 600
Preservation bath Professional 400
The vessel (owned or stolen) Fetch / mission —
Chrome serial (optional) Fetch / mission —
Components total ¥1,000

RitualGreatCircle.Name: Formula: Great Circle
RitualGreatCircle.Description:
Ritual Formula · Other · Magnitude 4–5 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Other · Magnitude 4–5 · General

Formula Item form: Restricted grimoire (bulky), with a Director veto callout

The story: Everyone you trust, in one room, for one night, doing something none of you are supposed to be able to do.

In plain words: With an initiate-grade leader and a full circle, one sealing may exceed the normal Magnitude cap by 1. It is a campaign lever, and it is easy to regret pulling it.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5, which is also what the circle itself costs in sanctum and study before it helps anything.
  • Scope — It supports another Working. On its own it does nothing except attract attention across the whole hive.
  • Seal — One night. Low: the circle breaks and the Working it supports goes wrong. Middle: the ceiling lifts. High: the ceiling lifts and Price is blunted a step.
  • Expires — It empowers exactly one sealing night, then it is over.

Payoff: Great-ritual ceiling break. With an initiate-grade leader and a full circle, one sealing may exceed the Magnitude cap by +1. A campaign lever; easy to regret.

Duration / upkeep: Empowers a single sealing night.

Scope notes: Supports another Working. Hive-wide detection.

Combat translation: None — a climax ritual beat. An interruption is catastrophic (Malice plus backlash).

Study time: 2 weeks (Magnitude 4) · 1 month (Magnitude 5).

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 8 / 10.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥6,000 (Magnitude 4) / ¥17,000 (Magnitude 5) (table below).
  • Sanctum: built sanctum at the Working's Magnitude — goal 12 / 15 (skip if owned).

Outer-ring ward Restricted 800 3,000

RitualScrubTheStain.Name: Formula: Scrub the Stain
RitualScrubTheStain.Description:
Ritual Formula · Unmaking · Magnitude 1–5 (equal to or greater than the stain) · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Unmaking · Magnitude 1–5 (equal to or greater than the stain) · General

Formula Item form: ritual scroll or datachip, annotated with stain taxonomy

The story: Scrubbing is the honest word. It takes hours, it hurts, and at the end the mark is gone or it is not.

In plain words: Strips a hung curse, a toxic mark, corrupted ward residue, or Taint (the cleanse ladder is in chapter 27). If the seal only half-works you still push the stain one step down its clock.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — This card's Magnitude must be equal to or greater than the stain you are scrubbing. Your copy is written at one Magnitude between 1 and 5, and that number is the ceiling on what it can clean.
  • Scope — Veil stains. Corrupted code, Overlay marks and hung daemons need Scrub the Ghost-Code instead.
  • Seal — One evening or one night, depending on the copy's Magnitude. Low: partial — one clock step. Middle: the stain is gone. High: gone, and Price blunted a step.
  • Expires — Immediately — the effect is instant at a successful sealing. There is nothing left standing to expire.

Payoff: Strips a hung curse, toxic mark, corrupted ward residue, or Taint (cleanse ladder in 27). A partial result reduces the stain one clock step.

Duration / upkeep: Instant at a successful sealing.

Scope notes: Veil stains. For corrupted code, Overlay marks, and hung daemons, use Scrub the Ghost-Code.

Combat translation: None — even mid-siege it's a Project sealing, not an encounter ability. No pool spend.

Study time: by the copy's Magnitude — 1 day / 3 days / 1 week / 2 weeks / 1 month.

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: Magnitude × 2 (2 to 10).
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥100 (Magnitude 1) / ¥300 (Magnitude 2) / ¥1,000 (Magnitude 3) / ¥4,000 (Magnitude 4) / ¥12,000 (Magnitude 5) (table below).
  • Sanctum: temporary at Magnitude 1–3; built sanctum at Magnitude 4–5 — goal 12 / 15 (skip if owned).

Components

Component Availability Magnitude 1 Magnitude 2 Magnitude 3 Magnitude 4 Magnitude 5
Solvent matched to the stain Street / Street / Professional / Restricted / Military 60 180 600 2,500 7,500
Specialty solvent and scrub-sink time Street / Professional / Professional / Restricted / Military 40 120 400 1,500 4,500
A sample of the stain Fetch / mission — — — — —
Components total ¥100 ¥300 ¥1,000 ¥4,000 ¥12,000

Price: failure can smear the stain onto the scrubber.

Counter: None — you are the counter. A rival can re-stain.

RitualDetoxDomain.Name: Formula: Detox Domain
RitualDetoxDomain.Description:
Ritual Formula · Unmaking · Magnitude 4–5 · General

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Unmaking · Magnitude 4–5 · General (threat-facing)

Formula Item form: hazmat grimoire or sealed datachip

The story: A whole block is sick. You go into the sick part of it and argue with what is making it sick, for a night, out loud.

In plain words: Pushes a toxic thin-place's agenda clock back one step. A failure makes the stain worse instead.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5, and it must be equal to or greater than the domain's stain or it cannot touch it.
  • Scope — Veil toxicity across a site. Wire-poisoned nodes need Scrub the Ghost-Code, at scale.
  • Seal — A night or a climax scene. Low: the stain deepens. Middle: the clock goes back one. High: back one, and Price blunted a step.
  • Expires — Instantly — it is a single clock move, not a standing effect. The domain pushes back on its next tick.

Payoff: Pushes a toxic thin-place's agenda clock back one step. Failure worsens the stain.

Duration / upkeep: Instant clock move; the site's fiction updates.

Scope notes: Needs Magnitude equal to or greater than the domain's stain. Veil toxicity; Wire-poisoned nodes need Scrub the Ghost-Code at scale.

Combat translation: A failed or worsening seal may spawn a toxic encounter. The Working isn't maintained in the fight. No pool spend.

Study time: 2 weeks (Magnitude 4) · 1 month (Magnitude 5).

Project Points (stages):

  • Study goal: 8 / 10.
  • Components: not a Project — pay the total from crew funds and run the fetch beats. Components total ¥5,000 (Magnitude 4) / ¥14,000 (Magnitude 5) (table below).
  • Sanctum: built sanctum at the Working's Magnitude — goal 12 / 15, or the toxic site itself if the Director allows.

Components

Component Availability Magnitude 4 Magnitude 5
Detox reagents Restricted / Military 3,500 10,000
Hazmat gear and containment Professional 1,500 4,000
A core sample (hazard mission) Fetch / mission — —
Components total ¥5,000 ¥14,000

Counter: The domain's agenda pushes back on its next clock tick.

Shared ritual rules (study, components, sanctum, sealing, detection, countermagic): @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.rulebook.JournalEntry.lbVxCseGwPRNJsZL]{The Veil — Ritual Workings}.

RitualThinPath.Name: Formula: Thin-Path
RitualThinPath.Description:
Ritual Formula · Threshold · Magnitude 3 · Elementalist only

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Threshold · Magnitude 3 · Elementalist only

Formula Item form: weather-stained tome or scroll tube

The story: Two places where the world is worn thin, and one night where you convince them they are the same place. You walk through, and the door shuts behind you.

In plain words: Opens a short path between two thin places you already know, big enough for the crew to walk through once.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Magnitude 3 buys one crew-sized crossing between known anchors. It also needs a sanctum rated 3 to seal.
  • Scope — Veil only, and both ends must be thin places you have studied or visited. The district notices automatically — Concord and corp clocks advance on any Magnitude 3+ Threshold Working in the Reach.
  • Seal — A night's work. Low: hung — the path opens somewhere you did not choose, or not at all. Middle: it opens. High: it opens and Price is blunted a step.
  • Expires — It collapses the moment the last of you is through. Either end can also be collapsed from outside with an Unmaking at Magnitude 3 or better.

RitualDomainAspect.Description:

Rare esoterica — found, never sold. Owning this Item does not let you cast: study it until the Director marks it learned, then have it present at sealing. Rituals never spend Essence, Conviction, or Resonance.

Threshold · Magnitude 3–4 · Elementalist only

Formula Item form: elemental almanac tome

The story: By morning it is raining ash on four streets and nowhere else, and the ash is not from anything burning.

In plain words: Paints Veil weather over a block for a session — ash rain, static bloom, soft gravity, whatever your element is. Things that match the weather get an edge; things opposed to it get a bane.

What this card's words mean here:

  • Magnitude — Your copy is written at Magnitude 3 or 4. The higher copy covers more ground and is harder to Unmake.
  • Scope — Veil only, over one block. Civilians feel it and talk about it, and the opposition will plan around it — this is not subtle.
  • Seal — A night's work. Low: the weather comes, wrong, and possibly on you. Middle: the block changes. High: it changes and Price is blunted a step.
  • Expires — At the end of the session, or after two dawns — your copy picks which. An opposing Domain Aspect cancels it early.

Payoff: Paints session-long Veil weather on a block — ash rain, static bloom, soft gravity. Matching elements and spirits gain edges; opposing ones take banes.

Duration / upkeep: One session, or until two dawns pass (the copy picks).

Scope notes: Veil only. Civilians feel it; the opposition plans around it.

Combat translation: Ambient edges and banes on the block. No pool spend to keep the weather.

The story: You do not summon this. You invite it, and then you spend the whole scene being the reason it has not turned around.

In plain words: Calls a greater-shape elemental for one climax scene. This is the "we brought a disaster on a leash" button.

  • Scope — A set-piece summon for one scene, not a servant for downtime — for that, use Long Leash. It is contested if anybody tries to banish it.
  • Seal — A night or the climax scene itself. Low: it arrives unbound. Middle: it arrives on the leash. High: on the leash, and Price blunted a step.
  • Expires — At the end of the climax scene or encounter. Then it leaves — or, if the leash failed, it unbinds violently on the way out.

Payoff: Calls a greater-shape elemental for one climax scene. The "we brought a disaster on a leash" button.

Duration / upkeep: One climax scene or encounter; then it leaves, or unbinds violently.

Scope notes: A set-piece summon, not a downtime servant (compare Long Leash). Price and Malice spike.
