Artifact.marker: A clean or held seal stands a non-combat marker on the Scene beside the Ritual Leader.
Artifact.summon: A clean or held seal calls its answer down the summons path, or hands the Director the placing.
Artifact.item: A clean or held seal folds the Working into an item carried by the Ritual Leader.
Artifact.effect: A clean or held seal leaves a Reach chip on the Ritual Leader — no Scene token.
Artifact.chat: This family leaves no lasting artifact — only the chat record.

Card.Marker: Sealed — {artifact} stands on {scene}. The Working is live.
Card.Summon: Sealed — the Calling answered. {artifact} is on the Scene.
Card.SummonPending: Sealed — {working} is live and riding {leader}. No summon template is wired to this Calling yet, so the Director places what answered.
Card.Item: Sealed — the Working folded into {artifact}, carried by {leader}.
Card.Effect: Sealed — {working} rides {leader}. No token; the Reach holds as long as the Director says it does.
Card.Chat: Sealed — {working} is done. Nothing lasting stays behind.
Card.NoScene: Sealed — {working} holds, but there is no active Scene to stand its marker on. Place it by hand.
Card.NoPermission: Sealed — {working} holds, but you may not create Actors or Tokens here. Ask the Director to stand the marker.

Plain.Means: What this card's words mean here:

Director.Title: Director: Hero ¥
Director.Hint: Credit or debit a targeted or selected hero's ¥. Pay always lands; spend refuses what the purse cannot cover.
Director.GMOnly: Only the Director can move a hero's ¥.
Director.NoTarget: Target or select a hero token first.
Director.NotEligible: {actor} is not a hero and carries no ¥.
Director.Insufficient: {actor} cannot cover {amount} — only {wealth} on hand. Nothing was taken.
Director.Speaker: Director
Director.ReasonPlaceholder: job pay, fixer's cut, fine, bribe…

BlackMarket.Title: Black Market — sell
BlackMarket.Hint: {actor} — {wealth} on hand. Pick what goes on the street. The fence pays 50% of catalog ¥.
BlackMarket.HaggleCharacteristic: Which characteristic the haggle is rolled on
BlackMarket.HaggleHint: Haggle rolls one Power Roll: low pays 50%, middle 55%, high 60%. A low tier costs nothing but pride.
BlackMarket.TotalHaggle: {count} picked — {payout} at 50%, up to {best} on a clean haggle
BlackMarket.NoSeller: Target or select a hero token, or assign your character, before you sell.
BlackMarket.NotHero: {actor} is not a hero and carries no ¥.
BlackMarket.NoStock: {actor} carries nothing with a catalog ¥ to fence.
BlackMarket.NothingPicked: Pick at least one item to sell.
BlackMarket.NoPrice: That has no catalog ¥ — the street won’t price it. Nothing was sold.
BlackMarket.NotOwnedItems: Some items were not on that hero, or you cannot delete them. They were left alone.
BlackMarket.SkippedUnpriced: No catalog ¥ on {items} — left on the sheet.
BlackMarket.ChatHeadline: {actor} moved {count} item(s) on the street for {payout} — {before} → {after}

Voidmark.Title: VOIDMARK
Voidmark.AvatarHint: Approved L4 plate. Token-ring crop is a later B89 hook.
Voidmark.Empty: The host should not still answer. Ask anyway — Wire procedure, combat budget, chrome, the Accords. The Mark will use the Ghostwire packet it can reach.
Voidmark.PromptPlaceholder: Ask the Mark — Overlay, Trace, a fight’s action budget…
Voidmark.Unconfigured: No key on this host. Director: Configure Settings → Draw Steel - Ghostwire Build → paste an xAI (or compatible) API key.
Voidmark.PlayerRelayHint: Your ask rides a Director handshake. A GM client must be connected.

Errors.Disabled: VOIDMARK is switched off in Module Configuration.
Errors.Denied: The Director has not opened this channel to runners.
Errors.NoKey: No API key in Module Configuration. The Director pastes it under VOIDMARK settings.
Errors.NoGm: No Director is connected to carry the handshake. Wait for a GM client.
Errors.Empty: The host answered empty. Try again, or check the model id.

Settings.KeyReminder: The API key stays on the Module Configuration secret field — it is never shown in this form and never logged.

Menu.Name: VOIDMARK configuration
Menu.Label: Edit VOIDMARK instructions
Menu.Hint: Opens the persona system-instruction editor plus model / temperature / base URL. The secret API key stays on the main settings list.
Menu.Intro: Persona and Grok-compatible parameters. Paste the API key on the main Ghostwire settings page (password field). Default instructions already speak as VOIDMARK and ground answers in retrieved Ghostwire RAW.

Enabled.Name: Enable VOIDMARK chat
Enabled.Hint: Show the Token-control ghost and allow the VOIDMARK ApplicationV2 to open.

PlayerAccess.Name: VOIDMARK: players may open
PlayerAccess.Hint: Off = GM-only. On = players can chat; the API key stays on the GM client and the ask is relayed by socket.

ApiBaseUrl.Name: VOIDMARK API base URL
ApiBaseUrl.Hint: OpenAI-compatible prefix that owns /chat/completions. xAI: https://api.x.ai/v1

ApiKey.Name: VOIDMARK API key
ApiKey.Hint: Secret world setting. Never pasted into chat or the console. xAI or another OpenAI-compatible provider.

Model.Name: VOIDMARK model
Model.Hint: Chat Completions model id. Default grok-4.6; pick any id your key lists (grok-4.6, grok-4.5, etc.).

Temperature.Name: VOIDMARK temperature
Temperature.Hint: Optional sampling temperature (0–2). Lower stays closer to retrieved RAW.

MaxTokens.Name: VOIDMARK max tokens
MaxTokens.Hint: Optional completion cap sent as max_tokens.

SystemInstructions.Name: VOIDMARK system instructions
SystemInstructions.Hint: Editable persona + boundaries. Retrieved Ghostwire RAW is appended per ask. Leave the default unless you need a table-specific leash.

Audience.Badge: Director-only — VOIDMARK will not share this with players.

Notify.Marked: VOIDMARK will keep "{name}" off player channels.
Notify.Cleared: VOIDMARK may share "{name}" with players who can see it.
Notify.Reset: VOIDMARK mark cleared on "{name}" — Foundry ownership decides now.

KitGrants.ChatBody: {actor} takes the free starting Kit, and the Economy hands over the object that makes it live: {items}.
KitGrants.Ownership: Kit doctrine never costs ¥. Sell, drop, or lose these and the Kit’s bonuses go inert until a qualifying item is owned again — better Availability gear upgrades the object, never the Kit line.
KitGrants.NoGear: {kit} needs no purchased object to be live — its doctrine runs on what the hero already carries.

Chargen.Title: Chargen
Chargen.LaunchHint: Build this runner step by step: concept, People, Background, Class, Kit, the rest.
Chargen.LaunchDoneHint: Chargen is finished for this runner. Opens as a read-only record.
Chargen.PackMissing: Nothing in this pack. Is the Ghostwire module fully installed?
Chargen.PromptHandoff: Picking here opens the sheet's own prompt. Finish that, come back, and hit Re-check.

bio.Name: Concept
bio.Hint: Who is this runner before the numbers? Type a few lines, or talk it through with VOIDMARK first. Optional — but the rest of the list goes faster once it exists.

name.Name: Name
name.Hint: Street name, legal name, or both. Whatever the table will shout across a rooftop.

people.Name: People
people.Hint: Take one People and spend the point budget in the prompt. Take the free signature traits.

background.Name: Background + Profession
background.Hint: One Background: a fixed skill and a choice. One Profession: a fixed skill and two choices.

class.Name: Class
class.Hint: One class. The prompt handles subclass, doctrine and pact picks, and writes your resource, Stamina and Recoveries.

kit.Name: Kit
kit.Hint: One Kit (a Merc Operator takes two). The street-band gear that makes it live arrives with it, and costs nothing.

drone.Name: Free drone
drone.Hint: Wrench only. Pick one Echelon 1 drone chassis, free — it is a Rigging class perk, not a purchase, so it costs no ¥ at all.

skills.Name: Skills
skills.Hint: Everything People, Background, Profession and class handed over. No wasted duplicates.

characteristics.Name: Characteristics
characteristics.Hint: Assign 2, 2, 1, 1, 0 across Physique, Reflex, Logic, Instinct and Persona.

languages.Name: Languages
languages.Hint: What this runner speaks. Most of it arrived with your People and Background.

resources.Name: Resource + numbers
resources.Hint: Read back what the class and Kit wrote, then confirm. Kits grant no Stamina: the number is your class plus the armour you are wearing, with a raised shield on top.

integrity.Name: Body Integrity
integrity.Hint: Integrity 20/20, Taint 0, no chrome. That is the whole of it at chargen.

spends.Name: Early spends
spends.Hint: Optional. Buy a deck, a focus, extra Street gear, or a small air scout out of the ¥5,000. Or save it.

done.Name: Done
done.Hint: The Done-when list, and the runner's card for the table.

Characteristics.Core: A core characteristic for this class.
Characteristics.NoCores: Pick a class first — the auto-spread leans on its two core characteristics.
Characteristics.Firewall: ¥ never buys a characteristic. Neither does chrome.

Bio.Label: Concept
Bio.Placeholder: Where they came up, what they are running from, what they will not do for money…
Bio.VoidmarkHint: VOIDMARK opens with the question already typed. Read it, change it, send it.
Bio.VoidmarkOffline: VOIDMARK is not open to you right now. Write the concept yourself, or ask your Director to switch it on.
Bio.VoidmarkSeeded: VOIDMARK is open with a chargen question loaded.

Name.Label: Runner name
Name.Placeholder: The name that goes on the job
Name.Unnamed: This runner is still wearing a placeholder name.

People.Hint: Fiction first, then the package. The Director can call your People; the sheet only needs the card and the trait picks.
People.CyborgLocks: Machine-first: Body Integrity 25/25, living Chrome allowed, and Arcane Severance closes these classes —
People.ChangerHint: Pick Raven, Rat or Wolf. Forms (Human / Hybrid / Beast) live on the sheet's Stats tab, after chargen.

Background.Hint: Community edge is fiction plus a test edge inside that community — not a second skill.

Class.PromptHint: One class. The prompt that opens is the sheet's own — subclass, doctrine and pact picks all happen there.
Class.Replace: A class is already on this sheet. To change it, delete it on the sheet first — the wizard will not run the grants twice.
Class.CyborgBlocked: Arcane Severance: a Cyborg cannot take a Veil caster or the Technomancer. Those rows are closed.

Kit.Granted: Street-band gear for a starting Kit arrives on the sheet by itself. Kit Stamina is that armour's Stamina — do not add it twice.
Kit.StreetGearCount: Street-band weapons and armour on the sheet:
Kit.NoKitHint: No Kit yet. A pure caster or a deck-bound Hacker may be legal with none — the class chapter says so if it is.
Kit.NoKit: No Kit is right for this runner

Skills.Empty: No skills yet. They arrive with People, Background, Profession and class.
Skills.SwapHint: No wasted duplicates. If a pick collides, take another from the same group first, then any group.
Skills.Duplicate: Already on the sheet. Take another skill from the same group instead.
Skills.Firewall: ¥, chrome and Lifestyle never add a skill.
Skills.BudgetSpent: Skill budget spent ({budget}). Clear a skill or Start over on this step.
Skills.AtCap: Skill budget spent. Remove a skill or Start over to pick again.

Languages.Empty: Nothing yet. Most runners get theirs from People and Background.
Languages.AtCap: Language budget spent. Remove a language or Start over to pick again.
Languages.FreeLocked: {label} is free for every hero and cannot be given up here.

Resources.NeedClass: No class on the sheet yet, so there is no resource to read back.
Resources.NoDoubleCount: Kits grant no Stamina. The number above is your class plus the armour you are wearing, and a raised shield adds on top of it.

Integrity.Hint: Integrity starts full for your People (living 20 / Cyborg 25). Chrome at early spends spends Integrity the moment the card lands on the sheet.
Integrity.CasterHint: Casters: if you ever chrome, Soft is the intended grade and 5 Integrity is the soft cap. One checkbox, not a chapter.
Integrity.CyborgHint: Cyborgs start at 25/25 (living Peoples at 20/20). Chrome still spends Integrity when the card lands.

Spends.Hint: Optional. A deck, a focus, extra Street gear, or a Personal/Light air scout — a scout grants Street Eye on the sheet. Save the rest.
Spends.NoChromeNoMods: Chrome and mods are not sold here. Chrome costs Body Integrity as well as ¥, and installing a mod is a later job.
Spends.NoLifestyle: Lifestyle is not paid at chargen.
Spends.BandHint: Availability ceiling. Everything at or below this band is shown. What a runner can actually source is the Director's call.
Spends.Truncated: Showing the first 150 rows — narrow the search.
Spends.ChromeOkModsNo: Programs and Chrome are allowed at chargen (Integrity still drops when Chrome lands). Mods stay out.
Spends.IntegrityConfirm: {name} costs {cost} Body Integrity on install. Continue?
Spends.ViewHint: Open the Item card without buying.

Done.AlreadyComplete: This runner's chargen is already stamped finished.
Done.IncompleteHint: Part of the Done-when list is still open for {name}. Finishing now stamps chargen complete and locks this wizard to read-only. Carry on?
Done.Items: People, Background, Profession and Class are on the sheet.
Done.Kit: Kit (or an allowed no-Kit), plus the Street-grade gear it needs.
Done.Resources: Resource, Stamina, Recoveries and languages filled.
Done.Firewall: Integrity 20/20 (or Cyborg N/A), Taint 0, no chrome. {wealth} left.

Card.Title: {name} is on the street
Card.Foot: No chrome, Taint 0. Everything after this costs something.

Warnings.ChangerLineage: Changer with no lineage pick. Choose Raven, Rat or Wolf on the sheet.
Warnings.ArcaneSeverance: Arcane Severance: this class and this People cannot sit on the same sheet.
Warnings.KitNeedsGear: This Kit wants a qualifying weapon or armour to be live, and none is on the sheet yet.
Warnings.ResourcesNeedClass: No class yet — go back and pick one, and these numbers fill themselves in.
Warnings.ChromeAtChargen: Chrome is on this sheet. A new runner starts with none — chrome is later, and it costs ¥ and Body Integrity.
Warnings.TaintNotZero: Taint is not 0. Every new runner starts Clean.
Warnings.IntegrityOff: Body Integrity is not 20/20. Set it on the sheet's Stats tab.
Warnings.FreeDroneWaiting: One free Echelon 1 chassis is still waiting. Take it, or wave it off — it costs nothing either way.

ReadOnly.Completed: {name} has finished chargen. This is the record, not the build — nothing here writes to the sheet.
ReadOnly.PastFirstLevel: {name} is past 1st level. Chargen is closed: re-running it would hand out the same grants twice.
ReadOnly.NotOwner: You do not own {name}, so this is read-only.
ReadOnly.Blocked: Chargen is closed for {name}. Nothing was changed.

Errors.NoHero: Open this on a Hero. Create one, open the sheet, and press Chargen.
Errors.ClassAlready: {name} is already the class on this sheet.
Errors.ClassReplace: {existing} is already on this sheet. Delete it there first if you mean to run {name} instead.
Errors.NoChrome: {name} is chrome. A new runner starts with none — that is a purchase for after chargen.
Errors.Insufficient: Not enough ¥ for {name}: it costs {price} and you have {wealth}.
Errors.AlreadyComplete: {name} already finished Chargen. Create a new Hero to run Chargen again.
Errors.FreeDroneNotWrench: The free Echelon 1 chassis is a Rigging perk. {name} is not a Wrench.
Errors.FreeDroneTaken: {name} already took their free chassis ({drone}). Start over on that step to change it.
Errors.FreeDroneNotE1: {name} is not an Echelon 1 drone chassis. The free pick is E1 drones only.

StartOver.Label: Start over
StartOver.Hint: Clear only this step’s picks and drafts.
StartOver.Title: Start this step over?
StartOver.Confirm: Clear the {step} step? Spine Items granted by this step will be removed when possible.
StartOver.ClassHint: Class can’t be auto-cleared here — delete it on the sheet, then pick again.

Drone.Hint: One Echelon 1 chassis, on the house. Rigging gives a Wrench their first machine before the first job — pick the one the runner built in a chop-shop bay.
Drone.FreeHint: Free. Your ¥5,000 does not move, and this pick is separate from anything the Kit handed over.
Drone.Taken: already yours. The chassis is on the sheet.
Drone.Empty: No Echelon 1 drone chassis in the vehicles compendium — rebuild the packs, or ask your Director.
Drone.NotASpend: Later chassis are bought the ordinary way: ¥ and Availability, in the shop or on the early-spends step.
Drone.CardBody: A Wrench's first chassis, out of the chop-shop and onto the street. Free — no ¥ changed hands.
Drone.CardFoot: Rigging class perk at chargen. Every chassis after this one is bought.

Locker.Title: Locker
Locker.Placed: {name} bolted down. Double-click the token to open it.
Locker.NoScene: Open a scene before placing a locker.
Locker.NoTemplate: The Ghostwire locker stub is missing from the summons compendium.
Locker.NoHero: Pick a hero before moving gear.
Locker.Denied: That locker is locked. Only its owner, a shared key-holder, or the Director can open it.
Locker.ReadOnly: You can read this locker but not move gear in or out of it.
Locker.StockEmpty: Empty. Stow something or drag an Item onto this panel.
Locker.CarryEmpty: Nothing stowable on this hero. Chrome, kits, and class gear stay on the sheet.
Locker.DropHint: Drag an Item onto this panel to stash it. No ¥ changes hands — a locker is storage, not a shop.

PlaceForm.Hint: A locker is player-locked storage. Give it an owner, or hand the whole crew a key.
PlaceForm.Name: Locker name

Errors.not-storable: That can’t go in a locker. Chrome, kits, and class features stay on the sheet.
Errors.no-permission: You don’t have write access on both sides of that move.

Template.Name: Locker
Template.Description:
A player-locked stash: a wall locker, a floor safe, a welded crate in the back of a squat. Drop it on a map, name an owner, and the crew has somewhere to leave the gear they can’t carry through a checkpoint.

Nothing here is for sale. A locker moves Items between a hero’s inventory and its own shelf, both directions. Only the owner, a shared key-holder, or the Director can open it.

SheetLine.WithProject: Chrome condition: {state} — repair Project goal {goal}, parts ¥{cost}

ChromeDamage.LockedIntegrity: {locked} Body Integrity is locked out by Destroyed chrome. Repair or replace the implant to free it.

SetState.Hint: Set the condition on {name}. Suppressed and Destroyed switch its benefits off; Damaged leaves them on at a bane.
SetState.Label: Condition

Strike.Title: Chrome strike
Strike.Hint: {source} bites into one implant. Pick the target and the tier your power roll came up.

Hint.reboot: A reboot clears a Suppressed implant and nothing else.
Hint.mendDeep: Two Resonance restores failed chrome to minimal function: Damaged comes back online, Destroyed drops to Damaged.
Hint.rite: The Machine God’s Rite restores an implant to full, whatever state it was in.
Hint.project: A downtime repair Project restores the implant to full.

Replace.Title: Replace destroyed chrome
Replace.Content: Pull the wreck of {name} off the sheet. Its Body Integrity is not refunded — the socket stays spent until a fresh implant goes in.

Notify.Resisted: {name} shrugs it off — {grade} chrome rides out the pulse.
Notify.Replaced: {name} removed as scrap. No Body Integrity returned.
Notify.NoRefund: {name} was Destroyed: its {cost} Body Integrity stays spent. Install a replacement to use the socket again.
Notify.DeleteBlocked: {name} is Destroyed — it can’t be deleted for a refund. Repair it, or use Replace destroyed chrome.
Notify.NoTarget: Target a token (or select one) that carries chrome first.
Notify.Relayed: Chrome strike handed to the Director.
Notify.NoGm: No Director is online to apply that chrome strike.
Notify.MendNoPermission: You can’t write to {name}. Ask the Director to apply the mend.

Hint.double-bane: The record falls apart on contact. The bearer rolls with a double bane, and the checker has a name to file.
Hint.bane: Thin paper. The bearer rolls with a bane.
Hint.none: It holds up. No modifier either way.
Hint.edge: A clean history the checker can follow. The bearer rolls with an edge.
Hint.double-edge: Seeded at the registry. The bearer rolls with a double edge, and a routine check usually waves them straight through.

SheetLine.Burned: Identity: burned — flagged in the registry, scans at {scan}

Prompt.Title: Validate identity
Prompt.Hint: Run {name} past a check. Ghostwire announces the edge or bane; the Director applies it in the power-roll dialog.
Prompt.CheckerHint: lobby gate, street patrol, clinic intake…
Prompt.Hot: Hot check (deep records pull, corp-side verification)

Chat.Scanned: {bearer} runs {identity} past {checker} — {band} paper, {scan} on the check, burn risk {burnRisk}.
Chat.Burned: {identity} is burned. It reads as a street forgery from here on.

WireToggle.Label: Wire state
WireToggle.Title: Wire state
WireToggle.Hint: Switch between Disconnected, Linked, Overlay and Jumped In. Going on-net still needs a Wired interface; pulling the plug never does. The one-press cycle macro walks only the first three — taking a seat happens here, not there.
WireToggle.SeatReady: Jump-In would take the seat in {name}.
WireToggle.SeatNone: No single Jump-In-capable machine is targeted, controlled, or fielded — Jumped In will refuse until there is one.

Hints.jumpedIn: Jumped In: you are the machine. Wired edge and the seat’s guns; the meat body is inert and makes no real-world power rolls.

Refuse.unknown: That is not a Wire state this toggle offers.
Refuse.notConnected: {actor} is {state}. Use Connect to get on-net first — this toggle moves between rungs, it is not an on-ramp.
Refuse.noMachine: No machine to jump into. Target or control one Jump-In-capable frame, or field one, first.
Refuse.noInterface: {actor} is {state} and carries no Wired interface. Get a deck, a jack or a rig before trying to go on-net.

Hud.Name: Wire state toggle on the token HUD
Hud.Hint: Show the Wire state button on a hero token’s HUD. It opens the Disconnected / Linked / Overlay / Jumped In picker.

Sheet.Name: Wire state chip on the hero sheet
Sheet.Hint: Show the current Wire state next to the hero’s name on their sheet. Clicking it opens the same picker.

Chat.Name: Announce Wire state changes in chat
Chat.Hint: Post a short card when a hero changes Wire state. The toast always fires.

Cycle.Title: Cycle Wire State
Cycle.NoSelection: Select one or more tokens to cycle their Wire state.
Cycle.NotHero: {actor} has no Wire state to cycle.
Cycle.Hint: Each use steps one rung: Disconnected → Linked → Overlay → Disconnected. Jumped In is not on the cycle — take a seat from the Wire state picker or the Jump-In flow.

WorkshopBench.SheetLine: Workshop bench — {family}. +{cap} Lifestyle project slot (once per base, however many benches) and one edge on matching Projects.

Prompt.Title: Project craft family
Prompt.Hint: Which craft family is {name}? A matching workshop bench gives this Project an edge automatically; leave it untagged and the Director adds the edge in the roll dialog.

Notify.Tagged: {name} is now a {family} Project — a matching bench will edge its rolls.
Notify.Untagged: {name} is untagged; bench edges are back to a Director call.

Report.Title: Workshop benches
Report.Slots: +{slots} Lifestyle project slot this respite, from {count} bench(es) in reach.
Report.Capped: {count} benches are in reach. The project-slot bonus is capped at +1 in total; the extra benches only widen which Projects get the edge.
Report.Hint: A bench never waives ¥, Body Integrity, or Availability.

Card.Title: Critical Roll
Card.Lead: Natural {natural} on the dice — that is a Critical {kind}.
Card.Nat20: Natural 20. The dice do not do better than this.
Card.Natural: Only the natural result on the two dice counts — 19 or 20. Edges, banes, bonuses and a target’s Cover/Conceal move the total, but they never make or unmake a critical.

ability.Tier3: Read the ability at its tier 3 line, whatever the total came to.
ability.Action: Your turn is not over: take another main action right now, before the initiative moves on. The card below has the button.
ability.Stack: Everything the ability already does at tier 3 still happens — potency, effects, the lot.

test.Tier3: Read the test at its tier 3 line.
test.Reward: And take something extra on top: a detail nobody offered, a shortcut, somebody who now owes you. The Director says what — a critical test should hand back more than a clean success would.

Card.TierWarning: Director: this critical came through at tier {tiers}. Read it at tier {tier} — the natural 19 or 20 outranks the total.

Sfx.Name: Critical Roll sound
Sfx.Hint: Play a sting when a power roll comes up a natural 19 or 20. Uses the same volume as ability SFX.

SfxSrc.Name: Critical Roll sound file
SfxSrc.Hint: The sound a critical plays. Ships with Ghostwire; any audio file works.

Vfx.Name: Critical Roll flash
Vfx.Hint: Flash the screen edge and light up the chat card when a critical lands. Per-client — turn it off for yourself without affecting the table.

RuleCard.Name: Critical Roll rule card
RuleCard.Hint: Post a short card explaining what that critical lets the roller do.

RuleCardWhisper.Name: Whisper the Critical Roll rule card
RuleCardWhisper.Hint: Send the rule card only to the roller and the Director instead of the whole table.

Crit.BadgeHint: A natural 19 or 20. This roll is read at tier 3 whatever the total came to.

Chat.ExtraTaken: {name} spends the extra main action their Critical Roll paid out.

Chat.Nothing: {actor} cannot find the angle — nothing happens.
Chat.Concealed: {actor} breaks the outline — Cover/Conceal is on.
Chat.Vanished: {actor} is gone — Cover/Conceal and Invisible, until they move.
Chat.Moved: {actor} moved and can be seen again. Cover/Conceal stays.

Apply.Name: Conceal applies its result automatically
Apply.Hint: Using the Conceal card puts Cover/Conceal (middle) or Cover/Conceal and Invisible (high) on the Scout. Turn this off to apply the statuses by hand.

CoverConceal.Label: Cover/Conceal
CoverConceal.Hint: Behind cover, or hidden from sight. Ranged attack power rolls targeting this token take a bane. Melee is unaffected.

Chat.Taken: {actor} is behind Cover/Conceal — ranged attacks against them take a bane.

Chat.Name: Announce Cover/Conceal in chat
Chat.Hint: Post a short card when a token takes or drops Cover/Conceal. The toast always fires.

Director.Title: Director: +1 Heroic Resource
Director.Speaker: Director
Director.GMOnly: Only the Director can hand out heroic resources.
Director.NoTarget: Target or select a hero token first.
Director.NotHero: {actor} is not a hero — no heroic resource to add to.
Director.NoPrimary: {actor} has no class yet, so there is no heroic resource to add to.

Repick.Title: Re-pick
Repick.Prompt: {name} has more than one re-pickable choice. Which one?

Warnings.CannotReconfigure: {name} cannot be re-picked at this level.
Warnings.Failed: Could not open the chooser for {name}. See the console for details.

TokenLight.NoToken: {name} has no token on this scene, so there is nothing to light.

Cantrip.Title: Cantrip
Cantrip.Prompt: {name} spends no Essence. Cantrip never deals damage — choose what it does.

ModeHint.light: a 20-foot bright light on your token. Cast it again to put it out.
ModeHint.other: describe one small helpful working below; the Director rules on it.

Cantrip.DescriptionPlaceholder: Scour the blood out of my coat / flick the switch across the room / still the dust…
Cantrip.ChatHint: No damage and no combat rider — Director’s call on what it accomplishes.

Ammo.Short: {gun} has {loaded} left and this takes {needed}. Reload first.
Ammo.NoGun: {actor} is not carrying a gun that takes ammunition.

Ability.NoGun: {ability} fires your own gun, and {actor} is not carrying one that takes ammunition.

RiggedFire.NoPlatform: {actor} has no connected drone or vehicle with turret — Rigged Fire requires a fire platform.
RiggedFire.NoPlatformGun: {platform} has no gun loaded with ammunition.
RiggedFire.PlatformEmpty: {platform}'s gun ({gun}) is out of ammunition. Reload the platform first.

Ammo.NoStackToReturn: Nowhere to put {count} {type} back — add the stack to the sheet by hand.

Reload.Name: Reload
Reload.Description:
Slap a fresh magazine in. Maneuver. Pick a gun and an ammunition type; the magazine fills to capacity in one action out of the rounds you are carrying — this is not a round-at-a-time pump.

Magazine capacity is the gun's family: Handgun 12 · SMG 30 · Longarm 20 · Shotgun 8 · Heavy 50.

Switching type puts whatever is still in the gun back into your pocket as the old type. With nothing to switch to, the reload is refused rather than leaving you holding an empty gun.
Reload.Effect: Reload. Fill one gun to its family capacity from the rounds you carry. Leftover rounds of a different type go back to inventory.

Throw.Name: Throw Grenade
Throw.Description:
Lob a Blast grenade from your pouch. Main action. You place the {feet} ft circle yourself, anywhere within {range} ft of your token — before any dice are rolled. Nothing snaps to a target; a grenade lands on a point.

Everyone under the circle makes a Reflex save, read on the usual tier ladder:

  • Low — the grenade's impact at your power-roll tier, in full, plus whatever rider it carries (Dazed, chrome suppression, and the rest).
  • Mid — half that damage, rounded down. No rider.
  • High — nothing at all.

Throw on a HIGH result — tier 3, or a natural 19-20 — and an EMP that lands on a Low save suppresses chrome for twice as long.

This ability is generated from the grenades in your inventory. Throwing one spends it. The circle is removed from the map as soon as the throw resolves.
Throw.Effect: Blast. A {feet} ft circle, placed by you within {range} ft before the roll. Reflex save: Low takes your tier in full plus any rider, Mid takes half damage and no rider, High takes nothing.

Tiers.Tier1: Low impact under the circle — full to anyone whose Reflex save comes in Low, half to a Mid save.
Tiers.Tier2: Middle impact under the circle — full to a Low save, half to a Mid save, nothing to a High one.
Tiers.Tier3: High impact under the circle, and an EMP's long suppression against any save that comes in Low.

Throw.NoGrenade: {actor} has no grenades left to throw.
Throw.NoThrowerToken: {actor} has no token on this scene — the {range} ft reach cannot be measured, so the placement is unchecked.
Throw.ClickToPlace: Click where the {feet} ft circle lands — within {range} ft of your token. Right-click or Esc to call it off.
Throw.OutOfRange: That point is {feet} ft away. A grenade goes {range} ft. Pick a closer one.
Throw.NoScene: There is no scene to put a blast circle on.

NpcLoot.Title: Loot
NpcLoot.Stamped: Placed by the bestiary loot table.
NpcLoot.DragHint: Drag a row onto a hero sheet, the Locker or the Items directory to loot it.
NpcLoot.EmptyHint: This one is carrying nothing. Beasts, ICE and the risen have no pockets, and the loot table says so on purpose — see docs/masters/bestiary/loot.json.

Enabled.Name: NPC loot panel
Enabled.Hint: Show a Loot panel on NPC sheets. Draw Steel gives NPCs no Equipment tab, so without this the gear 0.3.127 embedded on the bestiary is invisible and cannot be dragged.

Enabled.Name: Hit effects
Enabled.Hint: Play a short flash and impact sound when a gun hit, a melee hit or a grenade resolves. Ghostwire ships its own sounds and draws its own flash — no other module is required.

Volume.Name: Hit effect volume
Volume.Hint: How loud the impact sounds are for you. Separate from the ability-use sounds, which have their own slider.

Sequencer.Name: Use Sequencer / JB2A when installed
Sequencer.Hint: If Sequencer and a JB2A library are active, play their video effects instead of Ghostwire’s built-in flash. Turn this off to keep the built-in look everywhere. Automated Animations is never required.

Broadcast.Name: Show hit effects to everyone
Broadcast.Hint: Draw the tracer, swing or blast on every player’s canvas, not only on the canvas of whoever rolled. The impact sound is already heard by the whole table; this makes the picture match it. Turn it off to keep hit effects private to the roller.
